solution: Sort all 3N scores descending. Discard the N smallest outright -- each can be parked as the weakest member of some team without touching that team's median -- and pair up the remaining top 2N in order, so the medians are the elements at sorted positions 2,4,...,2N (1-indexed) and S is their sum. Correctness by exchange: in any optimal solution the largest score is wasted as a maximum, so it should shield the largest possible median, namely the second largest, and induction repeats the argument on the rest. O(n log n) time (or O(100) counting sort, since P_i <= 100) and O(n) space.
statement_summary: Given 3N students with individual scores, a coach must split them into N teams of three; a team's performance is the median of its three scores and the total is the sum over teams. The task is to report the largest achievable total. Both N and every score are at most 100, over up to twenty datasets.
notes: Exhaustive partition brute force over all team splittings agrees on 400 random cases with N<=3, plus the sample (17).
